cards.explanation: The answer is that they have not kept themselves separate. The leaders say the people of Israel “…have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples…” (Ezra 9:1). They say it reaches the priests and Levites too. That's the whole complaint, friends, right there in the first verse.

The answer is that they married women from those peoples. The leaders say “…the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land.” (Ezra 9:2). Marriage is how the report says the mixing happened, friends. The leaders put it that plainly.

The answer is False. The report says “…the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!” (Ezra 9:2). They weren't standing back, friends. They were out front. I think that's a heavy thing to hear.

The answer is True. Ezra says, “When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and cloak…” (Ezra 9:3). That's no polite "hmm, interesting," friends. I think this one hit him in the gut. It's a heavy moment, so let's let it be heavy.

The answer is everyone who trembled at God's words. Ezra says “…everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles…” (Ezra 9:4). They come to him, and they're not there for small talk. It's a quiet crowd, I bet.

The answer is that he kneels and spreads his hands to God. Ezra says, “…I fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God…” (Ezra 9:5). His first move is toward God, friends. After that comes the prayer.

The answer is enormous. Ezra prays, “…our iniquities are higher than our heads, and our guilt has reached the heavens.” (Ezra 9:6). It's stacked higher than he can reach, then higher than the sky. That's a man who isn't shrinking anything, friends.

The answer is because of their iniquities. Ezra says, “Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth…” (Ezra 9:7). The sword, captivity, pillage and humiliation all come back to that, friends. He says it about himself and his people, not about someone else.

The answer is new life and light to their eyes. Ezra says, “Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.” (Ezra 9:8). It's a bright line after a dark prayer, friends. Notice he says it even in bondage.

The answer is the kings of Persia. Ezra says, “…He has extended to us grace in the sight of the kings of Persia…” (Ezra 9:9). He says it even while calling them slaves, friends. He sees God's grace in the middle of that.

The answer is rebuild. Ezra says God gave them “…new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins…” (Ezra 9:9). Rebuilding is work, friends, and it's a gift too. They get to put the house of God back together.

The answer is daughters. The commandment Ezra quotes says, “…do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons.” (Ezra 9:12). It goes both directions, friends. Ezra says God gave this through His servants the prophets.

The answer is False. The commandment Ezra quotes says, “Never seek their peace or prosperity…” (Ezra 9:12). That's what it says, friends, plain as that. Ezra is repeating what God gave through the prophets.

The answer is so they could be strong and pass the land on. The commandment says, “…so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.” (Ezra 9:12). Strength and an inheritance for their sons are the reasons it gives, friends.

The answer is False. Ezra says “…You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this…” (Ezra 9:13). Less than deserved, friends, and a remnant on top of it.

The answer is that God would wipe them out, leaving no survivor. Ezra asks, “Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?” (Ezra 9:14). Notice it's a question he's asking, friends. The text doesn't answer it in this prayer.

The answer is righteous. Ezra prays, “O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous!” (Ezra 9:15). After all that confessing, friends, this is where he lands. He doesn't argue his case, he just says who God is.

The answer is True. Ezra says, “Here we are before You in our guilt, though because of it no one can stand before You.” (Ezra 9:15). He doesn't dress it up, friends. That's a heavy way to end a prayer, so I'll let it sit.
